Plan a nonright-triangle survey, examine any ambiguous sine-law case, and solve a periodic equation within a stated interval.
evidence: Explain an inverse function range and retain all solutions in the requested interval.
Justify a triangle-area or sine/cosine-law method and test geometric feasibility.
units.bridge: Angles and magnitude provide a second representation for complex numbers.

units.title: Complex geometry and conics
units.focus: Optional (+) extensions connect algebra to plane geometry.
learning: Use conjugates, moduli, rectangular/polar forms, and geometric complex operations; apply complex polynomial identities and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.
Derive ellipse/hyperbola equations from defining distances and construct an external circle tangent.
activities: Represent a complex product geometrically and compare rectangular and polar calculations.
Construct a tangent from an external point, then derive a conic equation from a distance description.
evidence: Check a complex quotient using its conjugate and explain a modulus/distance relationship.
State the number of polynomial roots with multiplicity and distinguish a conic definition from its sketch.
units.bridge: Directed magnitudes lead naturally to vectors and linear transformations.

units.title: Vectors, matrices, and transformations
units.focus: Optional (+) extensions organize directed quantities and linear systems.
learning: Represent vector components, add/subtract vectors, and use scalar multiples in physical models.
Operate on matrices, interpret determinants/inverses, solve matrix systems, and model plane transformations.
Use labeled matrices to represent and manipulate data, such as a network or a table of payoffs, in addition to representing plane transformations.
activities: Combine two invented velocity vectors geometrically and by components, explaining the reference frame.
Apply two matrix transformations in both orders, compare the images, and use an invertible matrix to solve a small system.
Encode an invented transport network or game-payoff table as a matrix, explain every row and column, and use a suitable matrix operation to answer a question about the data.
evidence: Explain dimensions and operation order; give a counterexample to commutative matrix multiplication.
Relate a determinant to area scaling and explain why a singular matrix cannot give a unique inverse solution.
Recover the meaning of a matrix entry from its labels and interpret the entries and dimensions of a resulting matrix operation in the data context.
units.bridge: Structured representations also organize multistage probability.

units.title: Probability distributions and expected decisions
units.focus: Optional (+) extensions separate long-run averages from guarantees.
learning: Use multiplication rules, permutations, and combinations to model compound events.
Build theoretical/empirical random-variable distributions, calculate expected values, and evaluate fair procedures and decisions.
activities: Build a probability distribution for an original two-stage game and compare exact and simulated expected payoffs.
Compare two invented service policies using probabilities, costs, and a stated nonfinancial constraint.
evidence: Explain why an ordered or unordered counting model applies and why probabilities total one.
Interpret expected value as a long-run mean, discuss spread/rare losses, and avoid presenting it as a guaranteed outcome.
units.bridge: Modeling choices require both quantitative evidence and a clear decision criterion.

units.title: A sustained mathematical investigation
units.focus: Synthesize optional extensions with core modeling and communicate limits.
learning: Use Cavalieri-style cross-section arguments to justify a sphere or other solid volume formula.
Select advanced tools for a design or decision, validate their use, and revise a model after critique.
activities: Compare corresponding cross-sections of solids to build an informal volume argument.
Complete an original design investigation combining a chosen geometric transformation, function model, or probability decision; present assumptions and sensitivity to changed inputs.
evidence: Distinguish an informal geometric justification from an empirical measurement check.
Deliver reproducible calculations, a defended model choice, a sensitivity check, and a limitation that materially affects the decision.
units.bridge: Review goals and readiness before selecting further study; no calculus entitlement is inferred.
